questions.question: The amount payable on maturity of a certain sum which is invested for 5 years at a certain rate per cent p. a. is Rs. 9,800 and the amount payable on the same sum invested for 10 years at the same rate is Rs. 12,600. If simple interest is offered in both cases, the rate of interest p. a. is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Simple interest remains constant for every year.

SI for 5 years = A₁₀ − A₅ = 12600 − 9800 = ₹2800

Principal (P) = A₅ − SI for 5 years = 9800 − 2800 = ₹7000

SI for 1 year = 2800 ÷ 5 = ₹560

Rate % = (SI for 1 year ÷ P) × 100 = (560 ÷ 7000) × 100 = 8%

**∴ The correct answer is 8%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Amount after 5 years (A₅) = ₹9800

Amount after 10 years (A₁₀) = ₹12600

**Formula Used:**

Amount = Principal + Simple Interest

Simple Interest (I) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

questions.question: Ramu can do a work in 36 days and Kanu in 32 days. If they work on it together for 12 days, then what fraction of work is left?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Work done by Ramu in 12 days = 12 ÷ 36 = 1/3

Work done by Kanu in 12 days = 12 ÷ 32 = 3/8

Total work done together in 12 days = 1/3 + 3/8 = (8 + 9) / 24 = 17/24

Fraction of work left = 1 − 17/24 = 7/24

**∴ The correct answer is 7/24.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Ramu to complete the work = 36 days

Time taken by Kanu to complete the work = 32 days

Number of days they worked together = 12 days

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total combined efficiency of Ramu and Kanu = 8 + 9 = 17 units/day

⇒ Total work done by both in 12 days = 17 × 12 = 204 units

⇒ Remaining work to be done = Total Work − Work Done = 288 − 204 = 84 units

⇒ Fraction of work left = Remaining Work ÷ Total Work

⇒ Fraction of work left = 84 ÷ 288 = 7/24

**∴ The correct answer is 7/24.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns

This topic follows the same logic as Time and Work, where inlet pipes fill a tank (positive work) and outlet pipes empty it (negative work).

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the exact ratio of the work done by each individual. If they work for an equal number of days, wages are distributed directly in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Alternate Day Work

When two people work on alternate days, combine their individual day works to find the total work completed in a 2-day cycle before progressing to the remaining amount.

questions.question: A man rows to a place situated 100 km away and comes back in 10 hours. He can row 12 km downstream or 8 km upstream in same time. What is the speed of the stream?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since time is constant, the ratio of Downstream (D) to Upstream (U) speed is equal to the distance ratio = 12 : 8 = 3 : 2.

Let D = 3x and U = 2x. The total round-trip time for 100 km is 10 hours.

100 ÷ 3x + 100 ÷ 2x = 10 ⇒ 50 ÷ 6x = 1 ⇒ x = 25/3.

D = 3 × 25/3 = 25 km/hr and U = 2 × 25/3 = 50/3 km/hr.

Speed of stream = (D − U) ÷ 2 = (25 − 50/3) ÷ 2 = 25/6 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 25/6 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total distance of one-way journey = 100 km

Total time taken for the round trip = 10 hours

Distance covered downstream in time t = 12 km

Distance covered upstream in time t = 8 km

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Speed of stream = (Downstream Speed − Upstream Speed) ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6c4ccab1ecab213e2770f33ed44d479849acd6615481a83aee4cfc067c2d9b76.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ The time taken to row 12 km downstream is the same as the time to row 8 km upstream.

⇒ Ratio of Downstream Speed (D) to Upstream Speed (U) = 12 ÷ 8 = 3 / 2

⇒ Let D = 3x km/hr and U = 2x km/hr

⇒ Total time for the round trip = 10 hours

⇒ (100 ÷ 3x) + (100 ÷ 2x) = 10

⇒ Dividing the entire equation by 10:

⇒ (10 ÷ 3x) + (10 ÷ 2x) = 1

⇒ (20 + 30) ÷ 6x = 1

⇒ 50 ÷ 6x = 1

⇒ x = 25/3

⇒ Downstream Speed (D) = 3 × (25/3) = 25 km/hr

⇒ Upstream Speed (U) = 2 × (25/3) = 50/3 km/hr

⇒ Speed of stream = (D − U) ÷ 2

⇒ Speed of stream = (25 − 50/3) ÷ 2

⇒ Speed of stream = ((75 − 50) ÷ 3) ÷ 2

⇒ Speed of stream = (25/3) ÷ 2 = 25/6 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 25/6 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed of Boat in Still Water

If downstream speed is D and upstream speed is U, then the speed of the boat in still water is calculated as (D + U) ÷ 2.

Speed of Stream

The speed of the water current (stream) is half the difference between the downstream and upstream speeds, given by the formula (D − U) ÷ 2.

Average Speed for Round Trip

When a boat travels equal distances downstream and upstream, its average speed for the entire journey is independent of distance and equals (2 × D × U) ÷ (D + U).
</p

questions.question: A man drives from Delhi to Nainital at x km/h and returns to Delhi by increasing his speed by 25%. His average speed for the whole journey is 93(1)/(3) km/h. What is the sum of the speed?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Let forward speed be 4 parts and return speed be 5 parts (due to 25% increase).

Average speed ratio for equal distances = (2 × 4 × 5) ÷ (4 + 5) = 40/9 parts.

Given average speed = 93(1/3) km/h = 280/3 km/h.

⇒ 40/9 parts = 280/3 ⇒ 1 part = 21 km/h.

Sum of speeds = 4 parts + 5 parts = 9 parts.

⇒ Total sum = 9 × 21 = 189 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 189 km/h.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fb4112a8bd8c00ed487c9e5fad12e25df6aa3e5f5108bdbc12cd5eabf15151b9.png] 

**Given:**

Initial speed (S₁) = x km/h

Return speed (S₂) = x + 25% of x = 1.25x km/h

Average speed for the whole journey = 93(1/3) km/h = 280/3 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed (for equal distances) = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂)

**Calculations:**

⇒ (2 × x × 1.25x) ÷ (x + 1.25x) = 280/3

⇒ 2.5x² ÷ 2.25x = 280/3

⇒ 10x/9 = 280/3

⇒ 10x = 280 × 3

⇒ 10x = 840

⇒ x = 84

⇒ Initial speed = 84 km/h

⇒ Return speed = 1.25 × 84 = 105 km/h

⇒ Sum of speeds = 84 + 105 = 189 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 189 km/h.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (Equal Distances)

When the distance travelled is equal for two different speeds x and y, the average speed is directly given by the harmonic mean: (2xy) ÷ (x + y).

Average Speed (General Formula)

For any journey involving unequal distances or multiple segments, Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time.

Relative Speed

When two objects move in opposite directions, their relative speed is S₁ + S₂. When moving in the same direction, it is |S₁ − S₂|.

Converting Speed Units

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply the speed by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.
</p

questions.question: A car covers a distance of 30 km and 250 metres in 25 minutes. The speed of the car in km per hour is _____.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total distance covered = 30.25 km.

Total time taken = 25 minutes = 25/60 hours.

Speed = Distance × (Inverse of Time)

Speed = 30.25 × (60/25) = 1.21 × 60 = 72.6 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 72.6 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

→ Distance covered = 30 km 250 m = 30.25 km

→ Time taken = 25 minutes = 25/60 hours = 5/12 hours

 
•

 Time = 25 minutes

**Formula Used:**

→ Speed = Distance ÷ Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed = 30.25 ÷ (5/12)

⇒ Speed = 30.25 × (12/5)

⇒ Speed = 6.05 × 12

⇒ Speed = 72.6 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 72.6 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Conversions for Speed

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply the value by 5/18. To convert from m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Average Speed

If equal distances are covered at speeds x and y, Average Speed = (2xy) ÷ (x + y). For variable distances, Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time.

Relative Speed

For two objects moving in the same direction, Relative Speed = S₁ − S₂. For objects moving in opposite directions, Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.
</p

questions.question: What is the ratio of the mean proportional between 24.2 and 7.2, and the third proportional of 2.8 and 4.2?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Mean proportional = √(24.2 × 7.2) = √(174.24) = 13.2

Third proportional = 4.2² ÷ 2.8 = 17.64 ÷ 2.8 = 6.3

Required Ratio = 13.2 : 6.3 = 132 : 63 = 44 : 21

**∴ The correct answer is 44 : 21.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Numbers for finding the mean proportional = 24.2 and 7.2

Numbers for finding the third proportional = 2.8 and 4.2

**Formula Used:**

Mean proportional between a and b = √(a × b)

Third proportional c of a and b ⇒ c = b² ÷ a

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f2803454e50d003177cf97d6cf249788dc03e29f564d8d73077a2c7e57893d31.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Mean proportional = √(24.2 × 7.2)

⇒ Mean proportional = √(242/10 × 72/10)

⇒ Mean proportional = √(17424 / 100) = 132 / 10 = 13.2

⇒ Third proportional = (4.2 × 4.2) ÷ 2.8

⇒ Third proportional = 17.64 ÷ 2.8 = 6.3

⇒ Required Ratio = Mean proportional : Third proportional

⇒ Required Ratio = 13.2 : 6.3

⇒ Multiply by 10 to remove decimals = 132 : 63

⇒ Divide both terms by 3 = 44 : 21

**∴ The correct answer is 44 : 21.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

If three numbers a, b, and c are in continued proportion (a : b = b : c), then b is called the mean proportional between a and c. It is calculated using the formula: b = √(a × c).

Third Proportional

In a continued proportion of three numbers (a : b = b : c), the third term c is called the third proportional. It is calculated using the formula: c = b² ÷ a.

Fourth Proportional

If four numbers a, b, c, and d are in strict proportion (a : b = c : d), then d is called the fourth proportional. It is calculated using the formula: d = (b × c) ÷ a.
</p

questions.question: A dealer allows 36% discount on the marked price of an article and still gains 25%. If the cost price of the article is reduced by 20%, then how much percentage discount should she give now on the same marked price to earn the same profit percentage as before?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let Marked Price (MP) = 100 units.

Initial SP = 100 − 36% = 64 units.

Initial CP = 64 ÷ 1.25 = 51.2 units.

New SP = (0.8 × Initial CP) × 1.25 = Initial CP = 51.2 units.

New Discount % = 100 − 51.2 = 48.8%.

**∴ The correct answer is 48.8%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Discount = 36%

Initial Profit = 25%

New Cost Price = Reduced by 20%

New Profit = 25% (same as before)

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP) × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

Cost Price (CP) = SP × 100 ÷ (100 + Profit%)

**Calculations:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/85e1cd974f1818f1c4d5409e8295ae6ba1d0f33e7905a0ee58a25556fd276679.png] 

⇒ Let the Marked Price (MP) be 100 units.

⇒ Initial Selling Price (SP) = 100 × (100 − 36) ÷ 100 = 64 units.

⇒ Initial Cost Price (CP) = 64 × 100 ÷ 125 = 51.2 units.

⇒ The new Cost Price is reduced by 20%, so New CP = 51.2 × 0.8 = 40.96 units.

⇒ The dealer earns the same profit of 25%, so New SP = 40.96 × 1.25 = 51.2 units.

⇒ (Notice that New SP = Initial CP, because reducing by 20% and increasing by 25% cancel out exactly: 0.8 × 1.25 = 1).

⇒ New Discount = Marked Price − New Selling Price = 100 − 51.2 = 48.8 units.

⇒ Required Discount Percentage = (48.8 ÷ 100) × 100 = 48.8%.

**∴ The correct answer is 48.8%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relation between CP and MP

A direct relationship formula connects Cost Price and Marked Price: MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%).

Successive Discounts

When two consecutive discounts of a% and b% are offered, the effective single discount is calculated as (a + b − a×b ÷ 100)%. It always results in a lower effective discount than their straightforward arithmetic sum.

Mark Up Percentage

Mark up percentage is the percentage by which the Marked Price is set above the Cost Price. Mark Up % = (MP − CP) ÷ CP × 100.
</p

questions.question: Let ΔABC ∼ ΔPQR andar(Δ ABC)over ar(Δ QPR)=25over144. If AB = 12 cm, BC = 7 cm and AC = 9 cm, then PR (in cm) is equal to:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of corresponding sides = √(Ratio of areas) = √(25 / 144) = 5 / 12

Since ΔABC ∼ ΔPQR, the corresponding side to AC is PR.

Therefore, AC / PR = 5 / 12

9 / PR = 5 / 12 ⇒ PR = (9 × 12) ÷ 5

PR = 108 ÷ 5 = 21.6

**∴ The correct answer is 21.6 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

ΔABC ∼ ΔPQR

Area(ΔABC) / Area(ΔPQR) = 25 / 144

AB = 12 cm, BC = 7 cm, AC = 9 cm

**Formula Used:**

When two triangles are similar, the ratio of their areas is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides:

Area(ΔABC) / Area(ΔPQR) = (AC / PR)²

**Calculations:**

⇒ (AC / PR)² = 25 / 144

⇒ AC / PR = √(25 / 144)

⇒ 9 / PR = 5 / 12

Similarity of Triangles

Two triangles are similar if their corresponding angles are equal and their corresponding sides are proportional. If ΔABC ∼ ΔPQR, then the ratio pattern strictly follows AB/PQ = BC/QR = AC/PR.

Area Ratio Theorem

The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is equal to the square of the ratio of any pair of their corresponding sides, altitudes, or medians.

Perimeter Ratio of Similar Triangles

Unlike the area ratio, the ratio of the perimeters of two similar triangles is directly equal to the ratio of their corresponding sides without any squared values.
</p

questions.question: The compound interest on a sum of money for 3rd year & 4th year are 1206 and 1809 respectively. Find the 5 years S.I on the same sum.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of consecutive years' CI gives the multiplier: 1809 ÷ 1206 = 3/2 ⇒ Rate = 50% (or 1/2).

CI for 3rd year = P × (3/2)² × (1/2) = 1206

⇒ P × 9/8 = 1206 ⇒ P = 1072

5 years SI = P × Rate × 5 = 1072 × 1/2 × 5 = 2680.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs.2680.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Compound Interest for 3rd year = Rs.1206

Compound Interest for 4th year = Rs.1809

**Formula Used:**

CI for (n+1)th year = CI for nth year × (1 + R/100)

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

questions.question:
The length of a rectangle is twice of its width. If the perimeter of the rectangle is 60 cm. Find its area in cm²?

a) 100

b) 200

c) 150

d) 300
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Length to Width = 2 : 1

Semi-perimeter = Perimeter ÷ 2 = 60 ÷ 2 = 30 cm

Sum of ratio parts = 2 + 1 = 3 parts

3 parts = 30 cm ⇒ 1 part = 10 cm

Length = 20 cm, Width = 10 cm

Area = Length × Width = 20 × 10 = 200 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 200 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b74945ddee5606e05cd638c53a3576c4d0690a4d2ab82efbbd5f604ac98dc232.png] 

**Given:**

⇒ Perimeter of the rectangle = 60 cm

⇒ Length (L) = 2 × Width (W)

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Perimeter = 2 × (L + W)

⇒ Area = L × W

**Calculations:**

⇒ Perimeter = 2 × (2W + W) = 60

⇒ 2 × 3W = 60

⇒ 6W = 60

⇒ W = 60 ÷ 6 = 10 cm

⇒ L = 2 × 10 = 20 cm

⇒ Area = 20 × 10 = 200 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 200 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Rectangle

The area represents the region enclosed by the boundaries of a rectangle. It is calculated by Area = Length × Width.

Diagonal of a Rectangle

The diagonal splits the rectangle into two congruent right-angled triangles. It is calculated using the Pythagorean theorem: Diagonal = √(L² + W²).

Properties of a Rectangle

A rectangle is a cyclic quadrilateral with four right angles where opposite sides are parallel and equal in length. The diagonals bisect each other and are of equal length.
</p

questions.question: Gold is 19 times heavier than water and copper is 9 times heavier than water. In which ratio gold and copper should be mixed so that mixed metal (alloy ) is 15 times heavier than water ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By applying the rule of alligation directly:

Weight of Gold = 19, Weight of Copper = 9, Weight of Mixture = 15

Ratio of Gold to Copper = (Mixture − Copper) ∶ (Gold − Mixture)

Required Ratio = (15 − 9) ∶ (19 − 15)

⇒ 6 ∶ 4 = 3 ∶ 2

**∴ The correct answer is 3 ∶ 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Weight of Gold = 19 times heavier than water

Weight of Copper = 9 times heavier than water

Weight of Alloy (mixture) = 15 times heavier than water

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aa30492f21a67d2df7818fef9a3a484107486e7a30e4eb9f09f63338279c6ea1.png] 

**Calculation:**

Let the quantity of Gold to be mixed be x units and the quantity of Copper be y units.

⇒ Total weight of the alloy = 19x + 9y

⇒ Total quantity of the alloy = x + y

⇒ Mean weight of the alloy = (19x + 9y) ÷ (x + y)

According to the given condition, the alloy is 15 times heavier than water:

⇒ (19x + 9y) ÷ (x + y) = 15

⇒ 19x + 9y = 15(x + y)

⇒ 19x + 9y = 15x + 15y

⇒ 19x − 15x = 15y − 9y

⇒ 4x = 6y

⇒ x/y = 6/4

⇒ x/y = 3/2

**∴ The correct answer is 3 ∶ 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rule of Alligation

It allows us to quickly find the ratio in which two ingredients at given values must be mixed to produce a mixture of a desired average value.

Weighted Average Formula

When two groups of quantities n₁ and n₂ have individual averages A₁ and A₂ respectively, the combined mixture average is determined by (n₁ × A₁ + n₂ × A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Replacement Method in Mixtures

If from a container full of pure liquid of quantity x, y quantity is drawn out and replaced by water n times, the remaining pure liquid quantity is x × (1 − y/x)ⁿ.

questions.question: The average of 4 numbers is 60 and the 1st number is 1 over 3 of the sum of the remaining three numbers. What is the first number ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of the 1st number to the sum of remaining 3 numbers = 1 : 3

Total ratio parts = 1 + 3 = 4 parts

Sum of all 4 numbers = Average × 4 = 60 × 4 = 240

Value of 1 part (1st number) = 240 ÷ 4 = 60

**∴ The correct answer is 60.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average of 4 numbers = 60

1st number = 1/3 × (Sum of remaining 3 numbers)

**Formula Used:**

Sum of observations = Average × Number of observations

 

 Total Sum of 4 numbers = 4 × 60 = 240
 
 
 
 
 1 part
 3 parts

 1st Number
 Sum of remaining 3
 
 4 parts = 240 → 1 part = 60

**Calculations:**

Let the four numbers be a, b, c, and d.

⇒ Sum of the numbers = a + b + c + d = 60 × 4 = 240

⇒ a = 1/3 × (b + c + d)

⇒ 3a = b + c + d

Substituting the value of (b + c + d) into the total sum equation:

⇒ a + 3a = 240

⇒ 4a = 240

⇒ a = 240 ÷ 4

⇒ a = 60

**∴ The correct answer is 60.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Basic Formula

Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Number of observations).

Weighted Average

If group 1 has n₁ items with average A₁ and group 2 has n₂ items with average A₂, Combined Average = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Ratio & Proportion Method

When a value is distributed in a specific ratio, the required part is calculated as: (Individual Ratio ÷ Total Ratio) × Total Value.

questions.question: What is the single discount equivalent to three successive discounts 10%, 15% and 20%?

Multiplying Factors for 10%, 15%, and 20% discounts are 0.9, 0.85, and 0.8.

Combined Multiplying Factor = 0.9 × 0.85 × 0.8 = 0.9 × 0.68 = 0.612

Equivalent Single Discount = 1 − 0.612 = 0.388

Given: Successive discounts d₁ = 10%, d₂ = 15%, d₃ = 20%

Relation between MP and SP

Selling Price = Marked Price × (100 − D₁)/100 × (100 − D₂)/100 × ... where Dₙ are successive discount percentages.</p

questions.question: A dealer offers a discount of 10% on the marked price of an article and still makes a profit of 20%. If its marked price is Rs. 800, then the cost will be
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct ratio between Cost Price (CP) and Marked Price (MP) is:

CP : MP = (100 − D%) : (100 + P%)

CP : MP = (100 − 10) : (100 + 20) = 90 : 120 = 3 : 4

Since 4 parts = Rs. 800 (Given MP), then 1 part = Rs. 200.

Therefore, CP = 3 parts = 3 × 200 = Rs. 600.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = Rs. 800

Discount = 10%

Profit = 20%

**Formula Used:**

SP = MP − Discount

CP = SP × [100 / (100 + Profit%)]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4392a88c8a077de8d68ffd1942060484659ba36301a8dd2d759cf48e538370fe.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Selling Price (SP) after 10% discount on MP:

⇒ SP = 800 − (10 / 100) × 800

⇒ SP = 800 − 80 = Rs. 720

⇒ Dealer still makes a profit of 20% on Cost Price (CP).

⇒ CP × 120 / 100 = 720

⇒ CP = 720 × (100 / 120)

⇒ CP = 720 × (5 / 6)

⇒ CP = 120 × 5 = Rs. 600

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP) unless specified otherwise. Formula: SP = MP × (100 − D%) ÷ 100.

Direct CP and MP Relationship

There is a direct relationship between Cost Price and Marked Price when profit and discount percentages are given: CP / MP = (100 − D%) / (100 + P%).

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount is calculated by the formula: (a + b − ab/100)%.

questions.question: A hollow sphere of internal and external diameters 4 cm and 8 cm respectively is melted into a cone of base diameter 8 cm. What is the height of the cone?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When an object is melted and cast into another shape, their volumes are equal.

Volume of Cone = Volume of Hollow Sphere

(1/3) × π × R꜀² × h = (4/3) × π × (R³ − r³)

4² × h = 4 × (4³ − 2³)

16 × h = 4 × (64 − 8) ⇒ 16 × h = 224

h = 224 ÷ 16 = 14 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 14 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

External diameter of the hollow sphere = 8 cm ⇒ External radius (R) = 4 cm

Internal diameter of the hollow sphere = 4 cm ⇒ Internal radius (r) = 2 cm

Base diameter of the cone = 8 cm ⇒ Base radius (R꜀) = 4 cm

Let the height of the cone be h cm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2198de5de461be990f53076b5e92060e74642b1b3d578b475a63a69d635fad0f.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a Hollow Sphere = (4/3) × π × (R³ − r³)

Volume of a Cone = (1/3) × π × R꜀² × h

**Calculations:**

Since the shape is completely melted and recast, the volume must remain conserved.

⇒ Volume of the Cone = Volume of the Hollow Sphere

⇒ (1/3) × π × R꜀² × h = (4/3) × π × (R³ − r³)

Canceling (π/3) from both sides:

⇒ R꜀² × h = 4 × (R³ − r³)

Substituting the given radius values:

⇒ 4² × h = 4 × (4³ − 2³)

⇒ 16 × h = 4 × (64 − 8)

⇒ 16 × h = 4 × 56

⇒ 16 × h = 224

⇒ h = 224 ÷ 16

⇒ h = 14 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 14 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume Conserved Concept

Whenever a 3D figure is melted and recast into another 3D figure, the volume remains exactly the same. The sum of the initial volumes equals the sum of the final volumes.

Volume of a Solid Sphere

For a fully solid sphere of radius R, the formula is Volume = (4/3) × π × R³.

Surface Areas of a Cone

Curved Surface Area = π × r × l and Total Surface Area = π × r × (r + l), where l is the slant height and l = √(r² + h²).
</p

questions.question: x = a cos θ and y = b sin θ then, b2x2 + a2y2 = ________
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Given: x = a cos θ and y = b sin θ

Substitute these directly into the expression b²x² + a²y²:

⇒ b²(a cos θ)² + a²(b sin θ)²

⇒ a²b²cos²θ + a²b²sin²θ

⇒ a²b²(cos²θ + sin²θ) = a²b²(1) = a²b²

**∴ The correct answer is a²b².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

x = a cos θ

y = b sin θ

**Formula Used:**

sin²θ + cos²θ = 1

**Calculation:**

⇒ cos θ = x/a

⇒ sin θ = y/b

Squaring and adding both equations:

⇒ (x/a)² + (y/b)² = cos²θ + sin²θ

⇒ (x²/a²) + (y²/b²) = 1

Taking LCM as a²b²:

⇒ (b²x² + a²y²) ÷ a²b² = 1

⇒ b²x² + a²y² = a²b²

**∴ The correct answer is a²b².**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities

1 + tan²θ = sec²θ and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ are the other two fundamental Pythagorean identities in trigonometry.

Equation of an Ellipse

The parametric equations x = a cos θ and y = b sin θ represent an ellipse. Eliminating θ yields the standard equation of an ellipse: x²/a² + y²/b² = 1.

Equation of a Circle

If a = b = r in the parametric equations, it becomes x = r cos θ and y = r sin θ, which represents a circle with the standard equation x² + y² = r².
</p

questions.question: In a school, the ratio of boy and girls is 4 : 5. When 100 girls leave the school then the ratio becomes 6 : 7. How many boys are there in the school?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the number of boys remains constant, equate the boys' ratio in both cases.

Initial Ratio (Boys : Girls) = 4 : 5 ≡ 12 : 15

New Ratio (Boys : Girls) = 6 : 7 ≡ 12 : 14

Decrease in girls' ratio = 15 − 14 = 1 part ≡ 100 girls.

Number of boys = 12 parts = 12 × 100 = 1200.

**∴ The correct answer is 1200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial ratio of boys and girls = 4 : 5

Number of girls who left the school = 100

New ratio of boys and girls = 6 : 7

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c1e3be31d76813a8c75a711f4d6372c6f2ea2a5e1de1264cd4236cfba31f23ba.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the number of boys be 4x and girls be 5x.

⇒ Number of girls after 100 leave = 5x − 100

⇒ New ratio = 4x / (5x − 100) = 6 / 7

⇒ 4x × 7 = 6 × (5x − 100)

⇒ 28x = 30x − 600

⇒ 30x − 28x = 600

⇒ 2x = 600

⇒ x = 300

⇒ Number of boys = 4x = 4 × 300 = 1200

**∴ The correct answer is 1200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Equivalent Ratios

Multiplying or dividing both terms of a ratio by the same non-zero number does not change its value. For example, a : b = ak : bk.

Constant Quantity Concept

In mixture or ratio problems, if one quantity is changed while the other remains constant, making the constant quantity equal in both ratios simplifies the calculation significantly.

Cross-Multiplication Method

When equating two fractions or ratios like a/b = c/d, their cross-products are always equal: a × d = b × c.
</p

questions.question: A man loses 25% of his money. After spending 60% of the remaining money, he has Rs. 360 left. What is the amount of money (in Rs.) he originally had?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the original amount of money be P.

Using the successive percentage multiplying factor method:

P × 75% × 40% = 360

P × (3/4) × (2/5) = 360

P = 360 × (10/3) = 1200

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Percentage of money lost = 25%

Percentage of remaining money spent = 60%

Amount left = ₹360

**Formula Used:**

Remaining Amount = Total × (1 − L₁/100) × (1 − L₂/100)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8d6d9d290681e4335cfc0d6c7f2b2ac8a0c601a391a39b6522a557198c558f27.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the original amount be 100 units.

⇒ After losing 25%, remaining amount = 100 − 25 = 75 units.

⇒ He then spends 60% of the remaining amount.

⇒ Amount spent = 60% of 75 units = (60 ÷ 100) × 75 = 45 units.

⇒ Remaining amount left with him = 75 − 45 = 30 units.

⇒ According to the question, 30 units = ₹360.

⇒ 1 unit = 360 ÷ 30 = ₹12.

⇒ Original amount = 100 units = 100 × 12 = ₹1200.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value is subjected to multiple percentage changes sequentially, the final value can be calculated directly using: Final = Initial × (1 − a/100) × (1 − b/100).

Base of Percentage

It is critical to identify the correct base for any percentage. Words like 'of the remaining' indicate the new percentage must be calculated on the newly reduced value, not the original starting total.

questions.question: When the price of sugar gets raised by 30%, a person increases his expenditure on sugar only by 12%. By what percentage (correct up to two decimal places) should he reduce his consumption of sugar so as to be able to maintain the same level of expenditure?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Let both the initial price and expenditure be 100.

New Price = 100 + 30 = 130

New Expenditure = 100 + 12 = 112

Required reduction on the new price = 130 − 112 = 18

% Reduction in consumption = (18 ÷ 130) × 100 = 13.846% ≈ 13.85%

**∴ The correct answer is 13.85%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Percentage increase in price of sugar = 30%

Percentage increase in expenditure = 12%

**Formula Used:**

Expenditure = Price × Consumption

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/706f9373854b97da9df0902a44acdcfc6899e002509a50eb6824d5d26b51821c.png] 

**Calculation:**

Let the initial price be 100 and initial expenditure be 100.

⇒ Initial Consumption = 100 ÷ 100 = 1 unit

⇒ New Price = 100 + 30 = 130

⇒ New Expenditure = 100 + 12 = 112

⇒ New Consumption = 112 ÷ 130 = 56/65 units

⇒ Reduction in consumption = 1 − (56/65) = 9/65 units

⇒ Percentage reduction = [(9/65) ÷ 1] × 100

⇒ Percentage reduction = 900 ÷ 65 = 180/13 = 13.846%

⇒ Rounding to two decimal places, it becomes 13.85%.

**∴ The correct answer is 13.85%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Percentage Change

The percentage change is calculated as the ratio of the difference between the final and initial values to the initial value, multiplied by 100. Formula: % Change = [(New Value − Initial Value) ÷ Initial Value] × 100.

Successive Percentage Change

If a quantity undergoes two consecutive percentage changes of a% and b%, the effective percentage change is calculated using the formula: Net % Change = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100.

Base Change Concept

If the price of a commodity increases by R%, the reduction in consumption required to keep the expenditure exactly the same is given by: Reduction % = [R ÷ (100 + R)] × 100.
</p

questions.question: An ice-cream cone with a lid has a total surface area equal to the area of another circle of certain radius. If the radius of the circle is equal to average of the slant height and the radius of the cone, then the ratio of the slant height of the cone to the radius of the circle is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total surface area of cone = Area of circle ⇒ πr(l + r) = πR² ⇒ R² = r(l + r)

Given R = (l + r) ÷ 2 ⇒ l + r = 2R

Substitute (l + r) in first equation: R² = r(2R) ⇒ R = 2r

Now, l + r = 2R = 2(2r) = 4r ⇒ l = 3r

Ratio of slant height to circle radius = l : R = 3r : 2r = 3 : 2

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 2.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Surface Area of an ice-cream cone with a lid = Area of a circle with radius R.

Radius of the circle (R) = Average of the slant height (l) and radius (r) of the cone.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6b570cd3c32de905e169e5ae7a0c6e53180a85b6797ee86c8f7e29b06dc7b495.png] 

**Formulas Used:**

Total Surface Area of a Cone = πrl + πr² = πr(l + r)

Area of a Circle = πR²

**Calculations:**

⇒ According to the given condition, Area of Circle = Total Surface Area of Cone

⇒ πR² = πr(l + r)

⇒ R² = r(l + r) ............. (Equation 1)

⇒ It is also given that R is the average of l and r:

⇒ R = (l + r) ÷ 2

⇒ Squaring both sides, R² = (l + r)² ÷ 4 ............. (Equation 2)

⇒ Equating Equation 1 and Equation 2:

⇒ (l + r)² ÷ 4 = r(l + r)

⇒ Since l + r is a strictly positive length, dividing both sides by (l + r):

⇒ (l + r) ÷ 4 = r

⇒ l + r = 4r

⇒ l = 3r

⇒ Substituting l = 3r back into the formula for R:

⇒ R = (3r + r) ÷ 2 = 4r ÷ 2 = 2r

⇒ The required ratio of the slant height of the cone (l) to the radius of the circle (R) is:

⇒ l : R = 3r : 2r = 3 : 2

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 2.**

**__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of a Cone

It comprises the curved surface area (πrl) and the flat base area (πr²). Therefore, Total Surface Area = πr(l + r).

Volume of a Cone

The volume represents the total internal capacity of the cone. Formula: Volume = (1 ÷ 3)πr²h, where h is the perpendicular height.

Slant Height Relationship

The slant height (l), base radius (r), and perpendicular height (h) form a right-angled triangle. By Pythagoras theorem, l = √(r² + h²).

Area of a Circle

The two-dimensional space enclosed by the boundary of a circle is its area, represented by the formula Area = πR².
</p

questions.question: If A and B are digits and A 3 + 8 B = 150, then the value of A - B is
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Look at the units column: 3 + B must give a sum ending in 0.

Since B is a single digit, 3 + B = 10 ⇒ B = 7.

This generates a carry of 1 to the tens column.

Look at the tens column: A + 8 + 1 (carry) = 15 ⇒ A = 6.

Therefore, A − B = 6 − 7 = −1.

**∴ The correct answer is −1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A3 + 8B = 150, where A and B are single digits.

**Formula Used:**

A two-digit number XY can be written as 10X + Y.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Expand the numbers A3 and 8B using their place values.

⇒ (10 × A + 3) + (10 × 8 + B) = 150

⇒ 10A + 3 + 80 + B = 150

⇒ 10A + B + 83 = 150

⇒ 10A + B = 150 − 83

⇒ 10A + B = 67

Since A and B are single digits, 10A + B represents the two-digit number AB.

⇒ This implies the two-digit number AB is 67.

⇒ By comparing the digits, A = 6 and B = 7.

⇒ We need to find the value of A − B.

⇒ A − B = 6 − 7 = −1.

**∴ The correct answer is −1.**

Place Value Expansion

A general two-digit number XY is mathematically represented as 10X + Y, where X is the tens digit and Y is the units digit. For a three-digit number XYZ, the expansion is 100X + 10Y + Z.

Cryptarithm Puzzles

These are mathematical puzzles where digits are replaced by letters. The key is to analyze the units column first and account for carries to the next higher place value.

Digit Reversal Rule

When the digits of a two-digit number XY are reversed to form YX, the difference between the two numbers is always a multiple of 9: (10X + Y) − (10Y + X) = 9(X − Y).
